content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged gray wolf frame. Host frame: the gray wolf sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a crab and a gray wolf. Head of the gray wolf, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: gray wolf body and legs, with its own dense fur over the whole body, colored as below; from the crab, as parts and materials on the gray wolf's own body — claws grown from the front feet, each front foot ending in a pincer held folded against the foot when the animal walks: heavy, knobbed, hard-shelled claws with a fixed and a moving finger, large and evenly sized with black tips; the gray wolf's own dense fur stays dense fur everywhere, and over the back and flanks it takes the crab's colors, gloss, surface texture and pattern; the gray wolf's body outline is unchanged. The donor's colors and sheen follow the host's own coat and body shape. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (rocky coast): dark back and light belly (strong countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing wolf-crab hybrid**
I'm planning a gray wolf silhouette with dense fur, keeping the wolf head fully visible and body and legs intact, while adding crab claws as the front feet with heavy, knobbed, black-tipped pincers folded when walking.
**Composing crab-wolf illustration**
I'm drafting a natural history illustration of a gray wolf with crab pincers on the front feet and crab-shell plating over the back and flanks, keeping bilaterally symmetrical limbs, dark-back light-belly countershading, and a plain light background with soft shadows.
**Refining hybrid creature design**
I'm preparing another generation to better integrate the wolf and crab features, adding fur over the body and shaping the front feet with folded pincer claws and crab-colored back and flanks.
